correctness.rationale: The 4D cross-polytope has 16 tetrahedral facets with normal epsilon/2 and facet three-volume 1/3; Cauchy projection formula gives X=1/16 Σ|epsilon·u|. On sorted absolute coordinates a≥b≥c≥h≥0 the sign average is max{a,(a+b+c)/2,(3a+b+c+h)/4}; 624 nonzero integer directions independently verify this finite identity. Piecewise cone extreme-ray argument establishes unique minimizing rays (1,1,0,0) under signed permutations (24 directions); Jensen equality gives exactly eight maximizing axes. Above √3/2 only the largest coordinate can control X, and disjoint S³ caps give the stated exact upper tail for 0<t<1−√3/2. At each minimum the exact local sign average has leading deficit 1/2 N(√2s,z,w), where N=max(|y|,|z|,|w|,(|y|+|z|+|w|)/2); its sublevel unit ball has volume 160/3 in y,z,w, rescaled tangent volume 80√2/3. The 24 isolated minima and area(S³)=2π² yield 320√2/π² t³+O(t⁴). The O(t⁴) follows from the uniform quadratic chart remainder, not sampling.
